title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
abstract: arXiv:2610.27500v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-\gamma Q^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, \gamma >0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Neha

translated_title: 一维孤子轮廓：增强的神经网络求解器与约束Deep Ritz方法
translated_abstract: 我们开发并比较了用于求解一维基态轮廓的增强神经网络求解器，这些轮廓是方程 Q″=bQ−γQᵖ（Q>0, p>1, b,γ>0）的解，即非线性薛定谔方程、广义Korteweg-de Vries方程和非线性Klein-Gordon方程的驻定轮廓方程。其显式的sech型解可作为误差计算和基准超参数选择的精确参考。我们通过引入基于Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt和L-BFGS精炼的高阶优化方法、Fourier特征PINN以及约束Deep Ritz（DR）表述，改进了标准的Adam训练物理信息神经网络（PINN）基线。在DR方法中，我们提出了两种新的神经网络表述，分别实现两种经典的变分刻画：一种是Nehari约束的Deep Ritz方法，其中解的高度（振幅）通过投影到Nehari流形上学习得到……
tldr: 该论文开发并比较了多种增强神经网络求解器（包括高阶优化精炼、Fourier特征PINN以及两种新颖的约束Deep Ritz方法），用于求解非线性薛定谔、广义KdV和Klein-Gordon方程的一维孤子基态轮廓，并以显式sech型精确解作为基准评估各方法的精度。
en_tdlr: This paper develops and benchmarks enhanced neural-network solvers—including Gauss-Newton/L-BFGS refinements, Fourier-feature PINNs, and two novel constrained Deep Ritz formulations—for computing one-dimensional soliton ground-state profiles of nonlinear Schrödinger, gKdV, and Klein-Gordon equations, using explicit sech-type solutions as exact references.
